trace: EXE High-NA (0.55 NA, 13.5 nm) builds on the 0.33 NA NXE EUV platform at the same wavelength. Imec documents an optical redesign and reworked patterning steps. The 2023 tool delivery, 2024 test prints and 2026 Intel 18A customer products mark separate stages on asml-exe-high-na-euv-scanner-platform.

ASML’s 0.33 NA NXE platform builds on the 2006 Alpha Demo Tool programme via the intermediate 2010 pre-production NXE:3100. The supplier history and Yen’s foundry experience support experimental continuity. The 2013 0.33 NA system introduction and 2017 NXE:3400B shipment preceded production readiness around 2018. See asml-euv-alpha-demo-scanner and asml-nxe-033-euv-scanner-platform.

TSMC’s N7+ process builds on base N7, inserting EUV for selected layers previously printed with immersion. Base N7 entered volume production in April 2018 and N7+ followed in Q2 2019. The N7 record links to TSMC’s 193 nm immersion work, tested on 90 nm chips in 2004 and used for 40 nm fabrication by 2008. See tsmc-n7-plus-euv-finfet-process, tsmc-n7-immersion-finfet-process and tsmc-193nm-immersion-lithography.

N2 is a distinct documented production process. TSMC’s 2024 report describes lithography development for N2 risk production, and the September 2026 High-NA announcement gives a later volume-use target. The new tsmc-n2-nanosheet-foundry-process record leaves scanner-model and process-family edges unasserted.

NTT had demonstrated reduced patterns with soft X-rays and multilayer mirrors by the mid-1980s (Kinoshita, SPIE 1742, printed pp. 576–577). ASML’s 2022 history describes this as early EUV work. The lane does not establish a specific transfer from NTT into the ASML Alpha Demo design. The existing Bell Labs record photolithographic-diffusion-windows establishes the earlier use of photoresist for semiconductor patterning, with an existing link to silicon-oxide-diffusion-mask. This batch supplies no bridge from those diffusion windows to a specific projection tool.
alternatives: Immersion DUV and standard EUV coexist. TSMC’s base N7 and N7+ show selective replacement at the process level, and ASML’s October 14, 2026 financial release discusses added capacity plans in both categories. It records 113 new and eight used systems sold during Q3 across lithography types and does not assign them to named fabs or establish tool delivery dates.

TSMC said in September 2026 that it intends to begin volume manufacturing with High-NA around 2030. Its proposed larger-mask transition has different milestones. A pilot line is targeted for 2031 and system readiness for advanced production by 2033. These targets and imec’s Leuven installation are distinct from the limited Intel production insertion already documented.

TSMC’s 2004 report characterizes 193 nm immersion as an alternative to the shorter-wavelength 157 nm path. This contemporaneous statement explains TSMC’s choice but does not identify a complete industry-wide chronology of 157 nm adoption or abandonment.
frontier: Find operator or conference qualification results naming the EXE:5200 site at Leuven. The March 2026 arrival release gave a Q4 qualification target, with no date of completed qualification established in sources checked through November 17.

Inspect TSMC foundry publications for a layer-specific NXE or ArF statement for N2 and an independently documented link from TSMC’s early 0.33 NA NXE research programme into a named N7+ manufacturing configuration.

Read the 1986 JSAP Kinoshita abstract and contemporaneous Bell Labs and Lawrence Livermore papers for precise dates, referenced predecessors and evidence of transmission. Investigate where projection exposure and the 1950s resist-window method are first documented together in production.

The existing Bell Labs oxide-window and oxide-mask entries concern a different step. Intel 4004, MOSIS and the semiconductor-foundry access lead concern distinct designs or services. No matching equipment or process milestone was found. EXE deliveries and commercial use are events on the platform record. N7 and N7+ are distinct process achievements from the same family.
coverage: Operator, supplier and participant evidence searched through November 17, 2026. The latest retained status observations are TSMC October 15, ASML sales October 14 and Intel–ASML September 8. Research-lab evidence has separate dates. The evidence is a selected set of production, research and equipment milestones, with reported plans and test results distinguished from in-fab production. Node labels, imaging wavelength, line width and pitch refer to different quantities. No worldwide priority claim is proposed.
